samples.question: The picture shows one horizontal RAIL near the bottom, drawn as a dark grey line crossed by short dark grey TICKS. The ticks are evenly spaced, the leftmost tick sits at the left end of the rail and the rightmost tick at its right end, and consecutive ticks cut the rail into equal UNIT CELLS. Above the rail stand five solid horizontal BARS, one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple, each drawn in its own row. A bar COVERS the stretch of rail lying directly beneath it, from the vertical line through its left end to the vertical line through its right end; how high up its row is drawn means nothing. The COMMON STRETCH is the part of the rail covered by all five bars at once, so it begins at the RIGHTMOST of the five left ends and ends at the LEFTMOST of the five right ends. The common stretch is never drawn and no single bar marks it: one bar fixes its beginning and a DIFFERENT bar fixes its end. A unit cell is counted only if the whole cell lies inside the common stretch, both of its ticks included; a cell that is only partly inside is not counted. No bar end ever lands on a tick. Every bar covers strictly more whole unit cells than the common stretch does, so the shortest bar never gives the answer. Pale grey vertical lines may show between the rows; they are decoration and mean nothing. Which bar begins the common stretch, which bar ends it, the colours of those two bars, how long each bar is, which row each bar occupies, and where along the rail the common stretch lies are each the answer no more often than chance allows. How many unit cells lie completely inside the common stretch? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 5.
